title: Multi-env Plan Preview + Policy Advisor (Conftest/OPA) for Private VPC IaC
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Problem: Teams deploying Redwood Private (VPC) frequently need to evaluate Terraform changes across multiple environments (dev/stage/prod) and validate them against our policy catalog before applying. Current CI pipelines run a generic `terraform plan` in a single environment and policy checks are scattered across repos, causing noisy PR feedback and occasional blocked upgrades.

Goal: Implement a standardized multi-environment plan-preview workflow in the IaC CI/CD that produces compact plan diffs per-environment and a unified Policy Advisor report (Conftest/OPA) with actionable findings. The flow should support: per-environment variable sets, drift-safe apply guards, an opt-in automatic remediation runbook link, and clear failure semantics for engineers vs. release automation.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI job `iac/plan-preview` runs for PRs and produces per-environment plan artifacts (dev/stage/prod) stored as build artifacts and a summarized HTML report.
- Conftest/OPA policy suite runs against the generated plans and emits a combined Policy Advisor report with categorized failures (security, networking, cost, compliance).
- A small rule-set will be enforced as hard fails for prod-targeting changes; soft-fail for dev/stage that creates advisory comments on PRs.
- Documented rollback and manual-apply guardrails for upgrades to TF modules; pipeline must include an explicit `apply` gate requiring a release engineer token.
- Integration tests that run against a mocked VPC module to validate the plan -> policy pipeline end-to-end.

Proposed approach:
1) Create a templated CircleCI/GitHub Actions workflow `iac-plan-preview.yml` that: checks out PR, runs `terraform init` with backend configured to use ephemeral workspaces, runs `terraform plan -out=plan-<env>.tfplan` for each env (env list comes from a repo-level `iac/environments.yaml`), converts plans to JSON (`terraform show -json`), uploads artifacts, and posts a concise summary comment to PR with per-env verdicts.

2) Introduce a `policy-advisor` step that runs `conftest test --input plan-<env>.json` against our Conftest rules. Normalize Conftest output into a single HTML/JSON summary with severity tags and suggested remediation links into our docs/Runbooks.

3) Add a lightweight adapter layer so Conftest output conforms to our Policy Dashboard schema. This adapter will be a tiny Python script `tools/policy_adapter.py` with unit tests.

4) Wire pipeline gating: for changes that touch `modules/vpc/**` or `modules/network/**`, the pipeline marks prod-targeting diffs as hard failure unless the PR includes the `release/allow-prod-apply` label and a designated approver has approved.

5) Create a small e2e harness under `test/iac/e2e` that uses localstack/moto style mocks (or terratest with a mocked provider) to exercise plan generation and policy checks without real cloud resources.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Running per-env plans increases CI time and cost; we mitigate by parallelizing jobs and only running full matrix on PRs that touch IaC paths.
- Conftest has limitations on plan JSON complexity; the adapter will normalize common patterns but some complex diffs (e.g., created resources with computed fields) will be classified as `needs-human-review` to avoid false positives.
- We intentionally keep prod rules strict to avoid risky rollouts; this may slow down developer iteration and will require clear on-call/approver UX.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Implement workflow and adapter in canary mode; run only for `dev` and `stage` envs and publish reports. (Low risk.)
- Week 2: Expand to include `prod` but as soft-fail advisory only. Collect PR feedback and tune rules.
- Week 3: Flip critical prod rules to hard-fail, add label-based apply bypass for release engineers, and publish runbooks.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Policy+Advisor+Design+(dev)
- Repo proposal: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-proposals/pull/27
- Draft runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/iac-policy-advisor.md

Release blockers:
- Need security team's sign-off on the prod hard-fail rule set (see security_review_required).  
- Conftest rule gaps: network CIDR overlap detection requires a new custom rego snippet we need to implement.

Metrics to track:
- False positive rate of policy checks (target < 5% in stage after tuning)
- Mean time to approve prod policy failures (goal < 4 hours)
- CI run duration and cost delta for IaC PRs (target < 2x baseline after parallelization)

Implementation tasks (tickets):
- Create CI workflow and per-env plan jobs
- Build policy_adapter and unit tests
- Add Conftest rule collection and CI caching
- Add e2e test harness and mock modules
- Update PR bot to post policy-advisor summaries

Expected owner: Infrastructure engineering (Liam Chen), with policy rules owned by Security (Janelle Ortiz) and Product input from Marco Silva.
